headline: The chief executive of South Korean streaming service Tving told lawmakers she presumes AI was used in a large theft of customer data and admitted she had not checked whether security spending was enough.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a regulator-level data breach with an AI claim, but the AI link is only the chief executive's presumption.
importance_line: Tving's customers face the risk that their personal data is in criminal hands, and Korean companies are being pressed to show they spend enough on security, but the AI claim is a presumption, police have not yet found how the intruder got in and no fine has been set.
summary: Seoul Economic Daily reports that Choi Joo-hee, chief executive of the South Korean streaming platform Tving, told a National Assembly audit on 13 Oct 2026 that AI was likely used in the large-scale theft of customer personal data ("That is what we presume"), adding that she did not make security enough of a priority to know whether spending was sufficient and that police are still investigating how the hacker got in. The Personal Information Protection Commission, South Korea's privacy regulator, plans to finish its disciplinary action this year, and its chairperson, Song Kyoung-hee, said a fine is unlikely to be cut just because damages were paid if the compensation is not meaningful.
notes: Seoul Economic Daily full text read; the English edition is AI-translated from Korean so quotes may differ from the original wording.
